teams.heading: Defending champions Fiji defeat Canada to reach Pacific Nations Cup final
teams.body: Defending champions Fiji have booked their place in the Pacific Nations Cup final after defeating Canada. The Flying Fijians will face Japan in the tournament's deciding match, presenting a vital opportunity to secure silverware. This regional success offers a timely boost for Fiji, who sit bottom of the log after three consecutive defeats, ahead of their next test against France.

teams.heading: Ben Youngs accuses RFU of having blinkers on after backing Steve Borthwick
teams.body: Ben Youngs has criticised the RFU for handing Steve Borthwick a contract extension following England's worst-ever Six Nations campaign. The former scrum-half claimed performance director Conor O'Shea and CEO Bill Sweeney have "blinkers on" after the board backed the head coach despite five Test losses in 2026, including a historic defeat to Italy. While Sweeney described the process as a "thorough and honest review," Youngs argued on his podcast that a long-term deal lacks accountability given Borthwick's current 59.6% win rate.

teams.heading: IRFU confirms there are no plans for Six Nations US fixtures
teams.body: The IRFU has dismissed speculation regarding the potential relocation of Six Nations matches to the United States. While World Rugby chief executive Alan Gilpin recently suggested that high-profile fixtures like Ireland versus Italy could help grow the sport stateside, the governing body clarified that no such discussions are taking place. An IRFU spokesperson stated that the union believes the competition holds a special place for supporters, noting that playing matches at home remains a central part of the tournament's enduring appeal.

teams.heading: Scotland women suffer heavy opening defeat against clinical World Cup finalists
teams.body: Scotland faced a difficult start to their WXV Global Series campaign on Saturday, falling to a 64-26 defeat against Canada at Hive Stadium. Despite tries from Evie Gallagher, Shona Campbell, Lana Skeldon and Rhona Lloyd, the visitors proved clinical, running in 10 tries to secure a dominant victory. While the result was a disappointment, interim head coach Dave Butcher’s side now shifts focus to their next challenge, where they will host New Zealand at the same venue.

teams.heading: BBC Wales confirms free-to-air coverage for the WXV Global Series
teams.body: Wales fans will have free-to-air access to the WXV Global Series after the BBC confirmed coverage of the upcoming campaign. Matches against South Africa and the USA, held at Cardiff Arms Park, will be available on BBC One Wales, iPlayer, and radio. WRU Chief Commercial Officer Tomos Grace noted that the women’s game is the "fastest growing part of the game" and remains central to the union’s strategy as the team looks to build on recent development.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus targets series victory in Baltimore against the All Blacks
teams.body: South Africa conclude their Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series in the United States, carrying a 2-1 lead into the final showdown. Rassie Erasmus has made two changes to his side, with Damian Willemse returning to start at full-back following Cheslin Kolbe’s broken jaw. Morne van den Berg also moves into the starting line-up at scrum-half. Having secured consecutive victories in Cape Town and Soweto, the Springboks look to maintain their physical dominance to close out the series.
